Checking the summary against the code

CodeRabbit Change Stack · Formbricks #8650 · Parth Pawar

I kept CodeRabbit’s layer model and focused on one review task in Formbricks #8650: check a summary, inspect the access guard, then get back to the call. The original already has summary jumps, viewed status and Focus.

What I sawWhat I changed
Controls compete above the code.File actions sit beside the filename. Display settings sit above the diff. Less frequent tools move into named menus, which adds a click when they are needed.
An empty pane narrows added code.This file has no previous version. I use Unified by default and a compact empty pane in Split. The original already offers Unified; this is a layout choice, not a new capability.
Six summary points share an 82-line range.Each point links to code the reviewer can inspect. One link opens the access guard; Return restores the call and reading position. Full wording and the whole function remain available.

Why I kept one code pane

Caller and guard side by side would leave both narrower at laptop width. I chose a return action instead. Keeping files and context visible also costs width, so Focus stays available.

What I kept

Layers, J/K, Z and separate seen/viewed states remain. Opening a file marks nothing viewed. I added Undo and made file versus layer context explicit.

What I would test

Ask developers to explain the access check on both screens, then find something the summary might miss. Compare missed branches and wrong turns. A precise link can narrow attention too much; the test needs to check that risk.

This prototype covers seven of 52 diffs at commit 23cdac2. Links are manually mapped. The PR is merged; Submit is disabled. Semantic diffs and modified-file review are outside this sample. I have not tested it with developers.
